g.text: Side effects — where the redundancy disappears
dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows · an idempotency key covers 3 of 3
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
STATE VS EFFECT, ON THE SAME RETRY
the same retry, two completely different outcomes
per-key state: window [12:08, 12:10)
recompute from the records → 8, every time
side effect: charge order 4 for 6
re-run → charged 12. There is no recompute.
why the difference
the state is a FUNCTION of the records; the charge is not
and the pipeline cannot tell
a timed-out charge that succeeded looks exactly like one that failed
Nothing the pipeline holds records that the charge happened — that fact lives in the payment processor.
So the pipeline has only two options: make the effect safe to repeat, or ask the external system whether it already happened. Those are the same
thing.
Step 1/4 — a side effect cannot be recomputed
The asymmetry is total. Recomputing window state gives 8 however many times you do it, because the state is a function of the records. Re-running
a charge gives 12, because the money moved and nothing in the pipeline knows. And the pipeline cannot distinguish a timed-out charge that
succeeded from one that failed — so it must either make repetition safe, or ask.
Side effects — where the redundancy disappears
dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows · an idempotency key covers 3 of 3
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
THE SAME RETRY, WITH AN IDEMPOTENCY KEY
the external system does the deduplication, because only it can
first attempt
charge("order-4", 6) → processor records the key, charges 6
the pipeline crashes before committing
it does not know whether the charge landed
the retry
charge("order-4", 6) → processor RECOGNISES the key
result
charged 6 total, and the retry returns the first attempt's answer
The key must be derived from the DATA (the order id), not generated at send time — a fresh key on the retry is a second charge with extra steps.
And this works only because the processor offers it. If the external system has no idempotency key, no amount of pipeline engineering supplies
one.
Step 2/4 — an idempotency key moves the dedup OUTSIDE
An idempotency key does not make the effect idempotent — it moves the deduplication to the only place that can see both attempts. Two requirements
follow, both in the note: the key must come from the data (a send-time key is useless), and the external system has to support it. The second is a
dependency you cannot work around from inside.
Side effects — where the redundancy disappears
dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows · an idempotency key covers 3 of 3
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
WHERE THE PIPELINE CAN CRASH WHILE CHARGING ORDER 4
crash before the shuffle
the record is re-sent and the shuffle recognises its id
dedup: covers
key: covers
crash after the shuffle, before the charge
the id is already past the dedup set; the replay sends a NEW copy that dedup has not seen
dedup: MISSES
key: covers
crash after the charge, before the offset commit
the charge happened; only the external system can know that
dedup: MISSES
key: covers
A deduplicating shuffle covers 1 of the 3 windows; an idempotency key covers 3 of 3.
This is where the redundancy from the previous concept disappears: for an AGGREGATION either guard sufficed, and for a SIDE EFFECT only the
external one does.
Step 3/4 — so dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows, the key covers 3
This is the concept's whole argument in one table. For a pure aggregation, dedup and an idempotent sink were interchangeable. For a side effect
they are not: dedup covers only the crash BEFORE the dedup point, and the two crash windows after it — record in flight, and charge completed —
are reachable only by the external system's own key. 1 of 3 against 3 of 3.
Side effects — where the redundancy disappears
dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows · an idempotency key covers 3 of 3
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
WHERE TO PUT THE SIDE EFFECT IN A FOUR-STAGE PIPELINE
stages: source → shuffle → aggregate → sink
effect at stage 1 (source)
a crash in any of 4 stages can re-run it
effect at stage 2 (shuffle)
a crash in any of 3 stages can re-run it
effect at stage 3 (aggregate)
a crash in any of 2 stages can re-run it
effect at stage 4 (sink)
a crash in any of 1 stage can re-run it
An effect at stage 2 is exposed to crashes in 3 stages; at the last stage, 1. That is a 3x reduction from placement alone.
It does not make the effect exactly-once — it reduces how many failures can repeat it, and keeps the computation above it pure and freely
retryable.
Step 4/4 — and isolating the effect at the boundary shrinks its exposure
Placement is the cheapest of the three mechanisms and the only one that needs no cooperation. An effect at stage 2 can be re-run by a crash in 3
stages; at stage 4 only 1 can reach it — a 3× reduction. And everything upstream stays pure, which means it can be retried without a thought.
